body: A maintainer (astra-2088) is working on the D510/D491 follow-ups; PR to follow. I checked open PRs, including drafts, and found no overlapping contribution. I will keep changes within the approved decisions and record any protocol or broader Permissive decisions separately.

Merged #2257 to main as `66da17e93cff18fde7ca412e7a500f9747c50d70` (reviewed head `16ff8474665e292f84305be2c18c58c678b73008`). This ships the D491/D510-compatible portion of this issue.

- Item 1 (file operations): receiving Windows executors recheck elevated setup on requests carrying the existing refusal, including full-disk operations that do not invoke the helper.
- Item 2: protected-level refusal now reaches skill/plugin capability-root discovery and skill resource reads, including full-disk profiles and locally under D491. The read path keeps the live refusal when the catalog was captured without a sandbox context.
- Item 4: ready remote environments without a usable sandbox get a startup notice with setup/upgrade steps; the session still starts. Deferred connections retain first-use refusal.

Four regression cases failed before and pass after using the existing harness/fake executor. Glitch Rust 1.99.1 clippy and focused tests passed (6 exec-server, 72 skills, 68 core, 20 integration, 1 developer-accounting). Exact-head independent Opus 5.5 High review round 3 APPROVED, followed by matching corbanu-security approval. All 42 applicable CI checks passed, including Windows clippy, native tests, integration, security probes, and credential canaries; no pending checks at merge. The PR has the complete validation record and release fragment. Native Windows fail-before and a real remote Windows/TUI exercise were not run locally.

Keeping this issue open for Travis's remaining decisions:
1. Items 1 (command launches) and 6: use a negotiated launch marker and actual per-process confinement provenance, or retain client prechecks. Recommendation: a separately signed-off, backward-compatible protocol design preserving unmarked Permissive launches. Other clients depend on this wire protocol.
2. Item 3 (PF-27-S06): correct executor-platform handling across all levels, or limit a repair to protected modes. Recommendation: complete target-platform correction after explicit security sign-off, because the full correction changes post-taint Permissive behavior beyond D491/D510.
3. Item 5: cache positive sandbox reports by URL, or keep fresh checks until executor identity and invalidation are specified. Recommendation: keep fresh checks; a time-only cache can fail open after an executor swap or setup change.

No protocol change or additional Permissive restriction is included in #2257. Protected discovery uses the existing discoverV1 capability, so older executors lacking it need updating. Startup checks are sequential; readiness-event notifications can be a later follow-up.
